Make for the opposite corner, while blocking your friends with your walls! Exit Strategy is played on a hex board, with a different color on each corner. On each turn you can either move your character 1 space or place a wall anywhere on the board to block off two edges. The goal is to try and reach your hex, on the opposite side of the board from where you start. The game is also a race, playing for places not just who reaches first. Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Be the first to reach the corner of your color, across the board from your starting position. If playing in Team Mode, all players on a team must reach their respective colors. On your turn, you can either move your character 1 space or place a wall anywhere on the board to block off two edges. If playing in fast mode, you can do both on your turn- move 1 space and place a wall- or you can skip placing a wall. Moving You can move to an adjacent hex, as long as there is no wall between the two hexes. You cannot enter a colored hex that isn't of your color. You can enter an hex already occupied with another character. In this case, you have to make a second move action, to an adjacent hex that isn't occupied by a character (meaning you cannot jump over multiple characters in a turn). Walling You have a limited personal supply for walls. The 2 parts of your walls must be between hexes (you can't place walls that would be half out of the board). You can never place a wall that would completely prevent a character from reaching its goal (you must always leave a legal path for every character). [Rating: 1/10] At first I thought the game was rated poorly because it’s a copy of Quoridor. But in reality, it wouldn’t deserve more even as a standalone game. Back in the 90s it might have been okay with kids, but nowadays it’s just a simple kingmaker game. Whoever sacrifices fewer turns to slow the others down — and is slowed down less by the others because they’re not in the lead — ends up winning. And that's the whole game.

[Rating: 3/10] I love the idea of a maze-making abstract game like this, but something in the execution just didn't really work. As you are racing to be the person who reaches your specific exit first, it is always in your best interest to be moving rather than slowing down a single player. While stopping the person in first does keep them from winning, you will also just be allowing the person who was in second to continue on towards their goal while you took a turn off from moving. Maybe this needs to be approached as a party game with tabletalk and yelling and whatnot, but the pairing of abstract strategy

[Rating: 3/10] Played on BGA, which may kill the little bit of fun.  What's left is pure kingmaking.

[Rating: 3/10] A multi-player version of Quoridor where you can move (the first to cross the board wins) or erect a barrier to impede someone else. Like Quoridor, the key is using your barriers to secure your own route home in a way that can’t be lengthened or blocked, and hopefully not having to spend turns working to prevent others doing the same. Multiplayer means total king-making in this respect though – which (frankly) is not good.

[Rating: 4/10] It's basically Quoridor.  Too similar to suggest this  BGA no undo   Google AmassGames for more and my Quoridor content ;)
